source_title: Gamma Communications plc Annual Report and Accounts 2019
availability_evidence: The issuer-hosted annual report states on page 46 that the Strategic Report was approved by the Board on 16 March 2020; the official PDF is preserved with its hash and extracted text in the source index.
observation: Gamma reported broad growth without a restructuring signal: revenue rose 15% to £328.9m, adjusted EBITDA rose 31% to £63.5m, gross margin improved to 50.6%, cash generated by operations rose to £54.0m and closing cash increased to £53.9m. Price pressure in Cloud PBX and weaker first-half Dutch performance were limited offsets, while the order book remained strong.
already_announced_exclusion: No qualifying restructuring or equivalent intervention had been announced by the cutoff; ordinary digital-platform efficiency work and acquisitions are not treated as target events.
review_note: The report supplies strong quantified contrary evidence across revenue, profitability, margin and cash, with only isolated product-price and Dutch trading pressure and no material intervention language.

source_title: Gamma Communications plc Annual Report and Accounts 2021
availability_evidence: The issuer-hosted annual report states on page 49 that the Strategic Report was approved by the Board on 21 March 2022; the official PDF is preserved with its hash and extracted text in the source index.
observation: Ongoing COVID-19 disruption delayed some customer decisions and new sales, and recruitment and wage inflation created modest pressure. Nevertheless revenue rose 14% to £447.7m, adjusted EBITDA rose 21% to £95.4m, Group gross margin held at 51.0%, cash generated by operations rose 28% to £89.8m and net cash increased to £49.5m. The business described a robust recurring-revenue model and a strong contracted order book.
already_announced_exclusion: No qualifying restructuring or equivalent intervention had been announced by the cutoff; pandemic support packages, acquisitions and ordinary operating-model optimisation are excluded from the target definition.
review_note: Pandemic, hiring and wage conditions justify modest pressure, but stable margin, strong organic growth, higher EBITDA, stronger cash conversion and positive net cash provide dominant contrary evidence.

source_title: Gamma Communications plc Annual Report and Accounts 2023
availability_evidence: The issuer-hosted annual report states on page 119 that the financial statements were approved and authorised for issue by the Board on 24 March 2024; the official PDF is preserved with its hash and extracted text in the source index.
observation: Gamma announced a late-2023 redundancy programme to consolidate proprietary-product development and combine the German and Dutch senior leadership teams. The completed exercise produced £3.3m of one-off severance costs and a £3.1m provision. It is excluded because it occurred before cutoff. Revenue rose 8% to £521.7m, adjusted EBITDA rose 9% to £114.3m, gross margin held at 51.2%, cash generated by operations rose 25% to £123.5m and net cash rose 46% to £134.8m.
already_announced_exclusion: The redundancy programme, product-development consolidation and German-Dutch leadership combination were announced and carried out in late 2023, so they are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: An explicit completed restructuring warrants high intervention pressure, but it cannot count prospectively; stable margin and exceptionally strong profit, cash generation and net cash provide very strong contrary evidence.
